newsitem.title: GERMANY: Airbus says aircraft output output to rise.
newsitem.headline: Airbus says aircraft output output to rise.

text.p: European planemaker Airbus Industrie said on Monday it would raise its aircraft output by 45 percent in 1997 to 183 units, increasing further to 220 in 1998.

In a statement issued from its headquarters in Toulouse and received in Bonn, Airbus said that its 1996 incoming orders were worth $34.4 billion, while orders on hand totalled $58.4 billion. Sales fell in 1996 to $8.8 billion from $9.6 billion.
Orders in 1996 for 498 aircraft give Airbus a world market share of 42 percent for aircraft with capacity of over 100 seats, the statement said.
Using its own stricter definition for firm aircraft orders, for which contracts have been signed, Airbus took 326 orders in 1996 from 31 customers worth $23.6 billion.
Airbus is a consortium of France's Aerospatiale and Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG, both with holdings of 38 percent, British Aerospace with 20 percent and Spain's CASA with four percent.
The four partners reached a preliminary accord last week to restructure the Airbus consortium into a limited liability company to meet the challenge set by newly-merged Boeing/McDonnell Douglas.
